For a corporate event, trade show, or gala in Las Vegas, a standard photo booth rental typically ranges from **$375 to $1,500+** , depending on the duration, technology, and level of brand customization.[[1]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVhFNFpESmZhbTFxGAo)[[2]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVdOek1USTVNbU5vGAo)

Cost expectations break down across different tiers and add-ons:

- Basic / Standard Digital Booths ($375 – $600 for 2 to 3 hours): Includes a digital-only or simple print setup (GIFs, boomerangs, text/email sharing) with a standard backdrop and an on-site attendant.[[1]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVhFNFpESmZhbTFxGAo)[[2]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVhkeE0yZG1iRGg0GAo)[[3]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVhkeE0yZG1iRGg0GAo)
- Premium & Interactive Booths ($600 – $1,200 for 3 to 4 hours): Includes custom-designed photo templates, premium physical props, higher-end lighting/enclosures, and live online galleries.[[1]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVdOek1USTVNbU5vGAo)[[2]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVdOdWNHdDJkekozGAo)
- Specialty & High-End Activations ($1,200 – $3,500+): Features 360-degree video booths, roaming iPad booths, robotic "Glambots," or green screen setups configured for high-volume trade shows on the Las Vegas Strip.[[1]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVhkeE0yZG1iRGg0GAo)[[2]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHBIaCgNwdnESE0Nnd3ZaeTh4Y1RZM2NWOTRhek0YCg)[[3]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHBIaCgNwdnESE0Nnd3ZaeTh4Y1RZM2NWOTRhek0YCg)

### Key Cost Factors to Keep in Mind

- **Corporate Customization:** Data collection (lead generation forms before users download photos), custom-branded physical wraps on the booth, and tailored corporate start screens usually add to the baseline fee.
- **Location Logistics:** Setting up inside major convention centers (like the Las Vegas Convention Center or Mandalay Bay) or high-end Strip resorts can sometimes incur extra fees for after-hours delivery, union labor/venue rules, or strict load-in/load-out windows.[[1]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVdOdWNHdDJkekozGAo)
- **Idle Time vs. Continuous Hours:** If your event has a gap (e.g., set up in the morning for a conference keynote, inactive during dinner, and active again for an evening gala), companies often charge an idle-time fee.[[1]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHRIbCgNwdnESFENnMHZaeTh4TVhkeE0yZG1iRGg0GAo)[[2]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHBIaCgNwdnESE0Nnd3ZaeTh4Y1RZM2NWOTRhek0YCg)[[3]](https://www.google.com/searchviewer/10?svid=CAwSHBIaCgNwdnESE0Nnd3ZaeTh4Y1RZM2NWOTRhek0YCg)

**Milestone Media** appears to be the strongest fit for a corporate or trade-show activation at **both Caesars Forum and Mandalay Bay**. It specifically advertises handling COIs, move-in/move-out schedules, freight, power, official contractors, and union-labor requirements for Las Vegas convention venues, including both locations.[1]

**Also worth contacting:**

- **Social Booth LV** — Offers photo booth activations at both Caesars Forum and Mandalay Bay and says it coordinates with Freeman or GES for convention logistics, including power drops.[2][3] Its public information confirms venue experience, but request written confirmation that it will complete your event’s EAC paperwork and provide the required COI.
- **MiHi Entertainment / Classic Photo Booth** — Listed as an exhibitor-services photo booth provider at Mandalay Bay and suitable for branded corporate events.[4] Confirm Caesars Forum availability, COI limits, additional-insured wording, and EAC handling before booking.
- **Let Me Shine Events** — States that it is insured and can provide a venue COI, with experience setting up at Las Vegas hotels and resorts.[5] Verify whether it has worked under convention-center EAC rules rather than only ballroom or private-event procedures.

### Requirements to put in writing

Ask each vendor to confirm:

- COI meeting the exact limits and additional-insured wording required by the venue and show organizer.
- EAC submission handled before the show’s deadline.
- Compliance with the official general contractor, commonly Freeman or GES.
- Union labor, freight, dock access, hand-carry, and material-handling rules.
- Power and internet requirements, including whether extra power must be ordered through the official contractor.
- Delivery, setup, attendant, teardown, and removal during approved move-in/move-out windows.

For Caesars Forum, EAC deadlines and COI wording can vary by event, hall, and general contractor, so the show’s exhibitor manual—not a generic venue statement—should control.[6] A useful vendor request is:

> “Please confirm that you will provide the venue-required COI, name Caesars Forum or Mandalay Bay and any required parties as additional insured, and complete all EAC paperwork by the show organizer’s deadline. Please also identify any Freeman/GES, union labor, power, freight, or dock charges separately.”

**Recommended first call:** Milestone Media for a convention-floor activation; Social Booth LV for a more traditional photo-booth package with established local venue coverage.
